To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vermicompost is more beneficial for soil fertility than composted rumen content.

the rumen content composted for nine month and vermicast obtained after passing the same through the guts of earthworms, showed a significant difference in terms of microbial activity, nutrient content and microbial diversity.
compost incubation with earthworms (i) increases microbial activity, (ii) improves microbial biomass and nutrient content of vermicast and (iii) increases the diversity of microbial community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of earthworms in the treatment of rumen content material, a byproduct of the meat industry, and the potential of vermicast and leached extract as a source of nutrients and microbial biomass.
a new approach to improve the quality of rumen content compost by means of vermicomposting, which may be useful for the recycling of rumen content in organic livestock farming.
the development of a new approach for the production of vermicast and its use as a microbial source of plant nutrients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the vermicast leaching extract, although containing the same microbial community as the vermicast and the composted rumen material, has a higher level of microbial activity, as indicated by the community level physiological profile (CLPP) analysis.
the rumen content composting process was not effective in improving the quality of the compost, but the vermicast leaching process did enhance the quality of the leached extracts.

vermicast leaching enhanced microbial activity and nutrient composition of the rumen compost, while the vermicast itself did not significantly alter the microbial and nutrient composition of rumen contents composted for 9 months.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vermicast leaching could be a promising method to enhance microbial activity and nutrient content of composted ruminal contents.
liquid incubation of rumen compost and vermicast enhances microbial activity and nutrient availability.

liquid incubation of composted ruminant material with earthworms and their leachate can enhance nutrient availability and microbial activity, thus increasing the potential for recycling rumen contents to agricultural soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that

liquid incubation of vermicast and composted rumen content extracts can significantly enhance the microbial and nutrient content of the composted rumen material, which could be used as an alternative source of nutrients and organic matter for plant growth.
the microbial community of the rumen is not completely lost during composting, as it is still present in the vermicasts, and can be reactivated in the liquid phase of the vermicast leaching extract.

the use of rumen contents for vermicomposting is a viable option, as it is able to support microbial activity, and the vermicast produced can be used as a source of organic matter for agricultural purposes.
